tldr: War premium is the whole ballgame: an 11th night of US-Iran strikes has Brent >$94 with Hormuz shipping stalled — bullish oil + metals, but it keeps the Fed hawkish into next week's FOMC (headwind for levered silver, HK tech, S-REITs).

Levered silver held ~$59.5 (two-day bounce) and gold rebounded ~1.8% to ~$4,152 on the safe-haven bid — relief for the book's highest-beta sleeve, but it's a geopolitical/inflation bid, not a rates thaw. Right-size leverage into the FOMC.

Rare-earth watchlist took a hit: Lynas' Q4 revenue MISS (A$289m vs ~A$391m) sent it to a 5-month low — the sell-the-news risk flagged yesterday. Structural thesis intact (IEA: $6.5T at risk; 10 Nov China curb-suspension expiry), so watch-and-wait, don't chase.

Regime firmed to a risk-on melt-up (riskOnProb 0.55): S&P at a record ~7,509, breadth broadening (~69% >200-DMA), ~$120bn fled cash into risk last week — yet CNN Fear&Greed reads 41 (Fear). Strong tape, cautious mood, stretched positioning.

Smart money unchanged (Q1 13Fs; Q2 due 14 Aug): Berkshire tripled GOOGL and re-entered airlines under Abel while cutting to 26 names; Amazon stays the tightest hedge-fund consensus long; Burry's chip shorts are the structural counter-view.
